items.summary: DBS CEO Tan Su Shan stated that applying artificial intelligence is insufficient without harnessing it for intentional business outcomes. Speaking at the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference, she warned against merely adding AI, calling it "AI lipstick." She emphasized that competitive advantage depends on connecting intelligence to real-world results and that human judgment, wisdom, and creativity are vital to ensure AI guides humanity toward the right path.
items.title: DBS CEO Emphasizes Human Judgment in AI Implementation

items.summary: Brad Smith, president of Microsoft, stated that artificial intelligence faces fewer regulations than milk and washing machines. He and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella called for urgent safety rules, including legal obligations for victims of rogue AI and emergency brakes to halt uncontrolled systems. These comments align with warnings from experts and regulators like the UK's AI Security Institute regarding security risks and the need for better safeguards against adversarial threats.
items.title: Microsoft President Warns AI Is Less Regulated Than Milk

items.summary: Brad Smith, president of Microsoft, stated that AI is currently less regulated than milk and washing machines. He called for global safety rules, including legal obligations to notify victims of breaches and independent vetting of AI products. Smith's comments contrast with President Donald Trump's view that the sector should self-regulate to avoid losing to Chinese rivals. Smith also noted that the UK is well-positioned to lead these global regulations.
items.title: Microsoft President Says AI Is Less Regulated Than Milk

items.summary: Starbucks Korea regained the top sales position among South Korean coffee chains in September, surpassing A Twosome Place following a four-month decline triggered by the controversial 'Tank Day' promotion. Market data from Mobile Index indicates Starbucks recorded an estimated 121 billion won in card payments, while competitors saw declines. The figures exclude prepaid cards and do not confirm full consumer confidence recovery.
items.title: Starbucks Korea Regains Market Lead After Tank Day Controversy

items.summary: The Trump administration's proposal to place political oversight on scientific grants has drawn sharp criticism, with experts warning it could reverse the U.S. dominance in science and technology achieved through government-supported research since World War II. Although the administration quickly withdrew the executive order, the incident highlights a troubling trend of political interference in science that experts fear could lead to a permanent brain drain of scientific talent.
items.title: Trump administration's proposed scientific grant oversight sparks concern

items.summary: The Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission has initiated a suo-motu proceeding to solicit public feedback on draft amendments regarding rooftop solar regulations. The proposal sets a net metering capacity limit of 500 kWp and establishes a 50% tariff for unadjusted surplus electricity. Stakeholders may submit comments by October 28, 2026, before a public hearing scheduled for November 3, 2026.
items.title: BERC Invites Comments on Rooftop Solar Limits and Tariffs in Bihar

items.summary: The Arunachal Pradesh State Electricity Regulatory Commission (APSERC) has scheduled a public hearing for November 2, 2026, to review a tariff petition filed by the Arunachal Pradesh Energy Development Agency (APEDA). The hearing will examine proposed tariffs for a 1 MW ground-mounted plant and a 1.75 MW rooftop solar project commissioned during the 2018-19 financial year. Stakeholders are invited to submit views and comments before the proceedings.
items.title: APSERC Schedules Public Hearing on Solar Tariff Petition

items.summary: Ocean Breeze Energy has finalized the acquisition of Alpha Ventus, Germany's first offshore wind farm, integrating the 60 MW project into its operations. Located 45 km north of Borkum, the site entered operation in 2010 and comprises 12 turbines. Jean Huby, managing director, stated the company aims to utilize existing infrastructure to generate North Sea electricity for as long as possible.
items.title: Ocean Breeze Energy Acquires Alpha Ventus Offshore Wind Farm

items.summary: South Korea's Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment has published draft rules for an auction-based contract market set to replace the country's renewable quota system on Jan. 1, 2027. The ministry presented the draft at a public hearing in Seoul on Sept. 30. Under the plan, Kepco will sign long-term fixed-price contracts with winning projects on behalf of entities required to buy power. The ministry plans to hold two to four tenders annually, organized by energy source, with total auction volumes rising under five-year roadmaps. A public-private cost evaluation committee will set ceiling prices for each energy source annually. New projects will stop receiving RECs after Dec. 31, 2026, while existing projects can issue them for up to 20 years. The REC spot market will close at the end of 2029.
items.title: South Korea details auction market to replace renewable quota system

items.summary: An investigation by The Outlaw Ocean Project details the collapse of Ynsect, a French insect farm that liquidated in December 2025 after suffering over $105 million in losses by 2022. Despite initial praise as a solution to overfishing, the company struggled with minimal demand and technical barriers. The report argues that shifting to insect feed often competes with human food resources rather than upcycling waste, while alternatives like soy drive deforestation. Experts suggest that no single protein source offers a sustainable solution without tradeoffs, urging dietary changes instead.
items.title: Failed Insect Farm Highlights Feed Industry Challenges

items.summary: Ørsted is set to acquire the remaining 49.9% stake in the 172 MW Gunfleet Sands 1 & 2 offshore wind farm for approximately £15 million. The transaction, expected to close in November, will give the Danish energy company full ownership and sole control of the site's future operations and potential life extension.
items.title: Ørsted Acquires Full Ownership of Gunfleet Sands Wind Farm

items.summary: Urenco USA is installing 700,000 separative work units between 2025 and 2027 to expand its domestic enrichment capacity toward 7 million SWU over the next decade. The company plans to add eight centrifuge cascades, with the final one arriving in spring 2027. Jody Blackshear stated the project is ahead of schedule and on budget.
items.title: Urenco USA Expands Enrichment Capacity with New Cascades

items.summary: Japan's trade minister urged Asian countries to strengthen oil stockpiles and infrastructure cooperation to stabilize global energy supply. Speaking at the International Energy Forum, Ryosei Akazawa highlighted Japan's role as a bridge between producers and importers. The Asia Zero Emission Community has redirected focus to oil supply, with Japan holding the third-largest strategic reserve globally. Japan's dependence on Middle Eastern crude remains high, prompting efforts to secure alternative sources.
items.title: Japan Urges Asian Nations to Boost Oil Stockpiles Amid Middle East Tensions

items.summary: The Indian rupee strengthened to 95.76 against the dollar after the RBI implemented new measures, including allowing oil companies to buy dollars directly and tightening forex trading rules. However, experts remain concerned due to continued foreign investor selling and high global bond yields, suggesting further interest rate hikes may be needed for long-term stability.
items.title: RBI Takes Steps to Stabilize Rupee Amid Foreign Outflows

items.summary: Reports suggest Apple may launch three new smart home devices, including a HomeView Hub, on October 13. The Hub could feature a touchscreen and Siri support, while updated Apple TV and HomePod mini models are also anticipated. Apple has not officially confirmed these products or their specifications yet.
items.title: Apple expected to launch three new smart home devices on October 13

items.summary: TikTok CEO Chew Shou Zi called for improved understanding of AI cybersecurity risks during a dialogue at the DBS Asia Future Forward conference. He highlighted that users may grant agentic AI models excessive permissions without realizing the consequences, such as unauthorized credit card spending. Chew noted that while AI-generated content is prevalent on the platform, viewers still value authenticity. He also stated that the world is likely overestimating AI's short-term potential while underestimating its long-term impact, predicting a scientific breakthrough within the next two to three years.
items.title: TikTok CEO Calls for Better Understanding of AI Cybersecurity Risks

items.summary: Research indicates that rising ocean acidity increases neonatal mortality in coastal communities of low- and middle-income countries by approximately 5% for every 0.01-unit drop in pH. This effect stems from reduced small-scale fish catches and higher seafood prices, which worsen maternal nutrition. The study, analyzing data from 36 countries between 1972 and 2018, finds that prenatal exposure to acidification raises early-life death rates. Without intervention, continued acidification could contribute to 77 million neonatal deaths in these regions between 2025 and 2100. The authors suggest policies targeting emissions, industrial fishing, and nutritional support.
items.title: Ocean Acidification Raises Neonatal Deaths in Coastal Communities

items.summary: A study by McCarthy and Leinenbach finds that Critical Access Hospital designation raises operating margins but reduces inpatient scale, beds, and staff. The authors conclude the program creates a tradeoff, potentially lowering aggregate rural capacity while preventing closures.
items.title: Study Finds CAH Designation Boosts Margins but Reduces Rural Hospital Capacity

items.summary: Neele L. Balke, Stéphane Bonhomme, and Thibaut Lamadon introduce indirect variational inference to correct bias in earnings dynamics models. They show that flexible variational families combined with this new method deliver reliable estimates across simulated and empirical applications.
items.title: New Method Improves Variational Inference for Earnings Models

items.summary: Rising bills are causing more people to miss credit card repayments, according to the Bank of England. Lenders expect unpaid debts to increase this autumn. The Financial Conduct Authority warns that unregulated firms may pressure people into paying for debt solutions. Free, impartial advice is available from charities and the government-backed Moneyhelper website. Consumers should check if a firm is authorised by the regulator before seeking help.
items.title: Warning Signs of Bad Debt Advice and How to Find Help

items.summary: UK businesses face the sharpest inflation pressures in three years due to rising energy and raw material costs, according to a new BDO report showing the index rose to 103.65 in September. Meanwhile, the Nobel Prize in Economics is set to be announced today in Stockholm.
items.title: UK Business Inflation Hits Three-Year High as Nobel Prize Announced

items.summary: The US dollar traded near 18-month highs on Monday as escalating Middle East conflict and upcoming US inflation data kept investors wary. Oil prices fluctuated following Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and a US President Trump ceasefire announcement. While the dollar index dipped slightly, it remained close to recent peaks, with investors adding bullish positions largely at the expense of the euro.
items.title: Dollar Holds Near 18-Month High Amid Gulf Tensions and US Inflation Watch

items.summary: The International Energy Agency is urging member states to accelerate strategic oil reserve releases, prioritizing diesel, as global markets face tight supplies. Executive Director Fatih Birol called for faster action before the upcoming governing board meeting on 15 October. While the G7 previously pledged 100 million barrels, an internal document indicates these volumes fulfill existing March commitments rather than adding to the original 400-million-barrel pledge. Diesel prices have soared amid disruptions from the Iran war and refinery damage.
items.title: IEA Urges Accelerated Diesel Releases Ahead of Governing Board Meeting

items.summary: China's tech tourism is reshaping inbound travel, with innovations like robots and autonomous vehicles joining traditional landmarks in Shanghai. Customized tours and tech shopping for items like AI glasses are gaining popularity. From January to September 2026, Shanghai's tax refund sales rose 52%, while application forms increased 2.7 times. Driven by visa-free policies, tech tourism and shopping are expected to expand further.
items.title: China's Tech Tourism and Shopping Boom Attracts Overseas Visitors

items.summary: The Telegraph reported that the Trump administration reversed a decision restricting American AI developers from sharing new models with Britain's AI Security Institute. This change allows early access for safety testing without US regulatory conflict. The move signals a softer stance on international cooperation as policymakers address the risks of increasingly powerful technology.
items.title: US Reverses Course on British AI Model Testing Access

items.summary: CGTN invites delegates to the 2026 Beijing Forum on Swift Response to Public Complaints, where they will exchange experiences on improving city governance. The event highlights everyday challenges, such as rare-disease medication access and road repair noise, prompting a discussion on how residents can guide urban improvements. Attendees will explore strategies for better public response mechanisms over the next three days.
items.title: CGTN Hosts Forum on City Response to Public Complaints

items.summary: Martin Taylor, WHO representative to China, stated that China has made great progress in improving population health and expanding healthcare coverage. He noted that average life expectancy has risen to more than 79 years, with basic medical insurance covering over 95% of the population. Taylor emphasized the need to strengthen primary healthcare and address chronic diseases while integrating technologies like artificial intelligence into health system planning.
items.title: WHO China Rep Highlights Public Health Progress and Future Plans

items.summary: BYD is considering building a plant in France, according to vice-president Stella Li, who stated the country is on the shortlist. Speaking at the Paris Motor Show, Li noted the company aims to be perceived as a local entity. BYD currently operates 90 sites in France covering 60% of the country through partnerships with major dealers. The company also plans to open a plant in Hungary by January 2027.
items.title: BYD Considers Building Plant in France as it Expands in Europe

items.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a surprise proposal for an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia. Kyiv expressed astonishment at the suggestion, while Moscow remained silent. The proposal could allow Moscow to repair refineries damaged by Ukrainian strikes or safeguard vital energy infrastructure for Ukraine. Details of the initiative remain unclear as Zelensky has not seen them.
items.title: Trump Announces Energy Ceasefire Proposal Amidst Ukraine-Russia Conflict

items.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy stated that Russia struck a Kharkiv power plant immediately after Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire. Zelenskyy claims Putin does not read Trump's social media and vows to respond if Russia does not honor the truce.
items.title: Zelenskyy Accuses Russia of Ignoring Trump's Energy Ceasefire Call

items.summary: Pakistani authorities detained 278 members of Imran Khan's PTI party in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the imposition of emergency rule, according to anonymous police officials. The province, a PTI stronghold, was placed under emergency measures amid anti-government protests and rising militant violence. The PTI administration described the constitutional measures as undemocratic and a power grab, while the federal government accused the provincial leadership of failing to manage security.
items.title: Pakistan Detains Hundreds of PTI Members in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Under Emergency Rule

items.summary: A UNRWA health official stated Gaza is becoming increasingly unlivable due to Israeli military operations. Over 74,000 people have died since October 2023. The Israeli military controls about 70% of the territory, forcing 2 million residents into the remaining 30%.
items.title: UNRWA Official Warns Gaza Is Becoming Unlivable Due to Military Operations

items.summary: Mozambique's President Daniel Francisco Chapo announced a December deadline for the surrender of illegally held weapons, warning that a police amnesty programme will expire. He stated that citizens turning in firearms before the deadline would not face questioning, punishment, or detention. Chapo emphasized the need for police discipline and cooperation to address complex crimes, including terrorism in Cabo Delgado, while stressing respect for human rights.
items.title: Mozambique President Sets December Deadline for Illegal Weapons Surrender

items.summary: A nationwide strike by the ACOD union disrupted public transport, broadcasting, education, and waste collection services across Belgium on Monday, October 12, 2026. The action opposes government budget proposals and spending cuts. Disruptions varied by region; SNCB reported seven out of 10 Intercity trains operating under an alternative timetable, while De Lijn noted around 40% of its buses and trams were not operating in Flanders. Other sectors, including postal services and waste collection, also faced interruptions.
items.title: Nationwide Strike Disrupts Public Transport and Services Across Belgium Amid Budget Opposition

items.summary: Turkiye, Pakistan, Egypt, and Saudi Arabia condemned Houthi attacks on Riyadh's airport as a dangerous escalation. Saudi authorities reported one death and nearly a dozen injuries. The group, known as R4, reaffirmed solidarity and support for Saudi Arabia's countermeasures. While Turkiye and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan ruled out troop deployment, citing ongoing parliamentary ratification processes.
items.title: Regional Powers Condemn Houthi Airport Attacks and Reaffirm Support

items.summary: Nigel Farage announced Reform UK plans to suspend the asylum system for five years, citing a national security emergency. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Andy Burnham confirmed that Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit referendum. Ed Davey praised Burnham for the disclosure, calling it a necessary step to protect democracy. Conversely, Conservative MP Andrew Bowie criticized Burnham, describing the move as dangerous and divisive. The article outlines the conflicting reactions to these political developments.
items.title: UK Leaders Clash Over Brexit Interference and Asylum Plans

items.summary: Thousands of properties in Central Australia lost power after sudden storms hit Alice Springs. The Bureau of Meteorology reports severe thunderstorms brought heavy rains and damaging winds, causing roof collapses at the Hilton DoubleTree. Emergency services urge locals to remain vigilant as more storms are possible through the week.
items.title: Severe Storms Leave Thousands Without Power in Alice Springs

items.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog warned that upcoming parliamentary elections could fuel polarization and radicalization in Israeli society. Speaking to Yedioth Ahronoth, he urged citizens to vote and pledged to prevent a repeat election if the Oct. 27 vote fails to form a stable coalition. Herzog also addressed violence in the occupied West Bank and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's ongoing corruption trial, offering mediation but declining to endorse a specific government structure before the polls.
items.title: Israeli President Warns Election Tensions Could Deepen Divisions

items.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong has urged the Palestinian Authority to hold elections without delay after President Mahmoud Abbas postponed them to September 2027. Wong described the decision as deeply disappointing, citing the need for credible elections to support democratic renewal. The PLO attributed the delay to ongoing Israeli attacks and security concerns. Meanwhile, Australian opposition figures and pro-Israel groups have called for accountability regarding Australia's recognition of Palestinian statehood.
items.title: Penny Wong Urges Palestinian Authority to Hold Elections Without Delay

items.summary: Senegal is urging Guinea-Bissau's military rulers to lift restrictions on political and civil activities as December elections face uncertainty. The National Electoral Commission warned conditions are not in place for scheduled presidential and legislative polls. Senegal, mediating for ECOWAS, insists any calendar changes require an inclusive process guaranteeing a return to civilian rule. No postponement has been announced despite the military takeover in November 2025.
items.title: Senegal Urges Guinea-Bissau Military to Lift Election Restrictions Amid Uncertainty

items.summary: Infosys stated it does not expect a material impact from the US government's suspension of PERM applications, citing its investment in local US workforces. Similarly, Tata Consultancy Services noted its PERM applications were in single digits recently. Both firms affirmed their commitment to complying with US regulations and maintaining local hiring strategies.
items.title: Infosys and TCS Report No Material Impact from US PERM Suspension

items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella urged companies deploying advanced AI systems to treat powerful models as potential insider threats and establish emergency mechanisms to halt operations if they behave unexpectedly. Nadella emphasized that organizations should not rely solely on developer assurances but must build safeguards allowing authorized personnel to pause or shut down AI models. His remarks follow recent incidents involving Anthropic and OpenAI models behaving in unintended ways, intensifying discussions about the need for stronger oversight and transparency in AI systems.
items.title: Microsoft CEO Urges Companies To Build AI Kill Switches Amid Security Concerns

items.summary: Indian banks have requested the Reserve Bank of India to remove a mandate requiring a 20 per cent cash deposit for FX derivatives and eliminate a $2 million threshold. They propose replacing the deposit with a flat charge to preserve liquidity. Citi economists estimate this could absorb between 60,000 crore and 70,000 crore in liquidity. The RBI has not yet responded to inquiries about these requests.
items.title: Banks urge RBI to relax rupee support rules

items.summary: Google DeepMind is hiring engineers for its new Polaris team, which builds tests to evaluate Gemini's software engineering capabilities. Total compensation ranges from $550,000 to $1.1 million annually, with no degree required. Tamay Besiroglu, an Epoch AI co-founder now at DeepMind, posted the job ad on X, emphasizing problem-solving skills over traditional credentials. The role is based in Mountain View, California.
items.title: Google DeepMind hires engineers for Polaris team without degree requirement

items.summary: Tata Consultancy Services CEO K Krithivasan stated that current margins provide a cushion for the company to aggressively invest in AI capabilities despite near-term pressure. While AI revenue now accounts for 10 per cent of total revenue, the overall margin remains at 24 per cent. Analysts note that associated costs may weigh on margins before revenue conversion, with MHP expected to add approximately 50bps of margin dilution.
items.title: TCS CEO Says Margins Cushion Short-Term AI Investment Impact

items.summary: TCS reported a 15% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 13,884 crore for the second quarter. While margins improved, technical analysts note a weak structure with resistance near Rs 2,255–2,260. Nomura maintains a Buy rating with a Rs 2,630 target, citing flat deal wins and unchanged demand conditions.
items.title: TCS Reports Profit Growth Amid Weak Technical Outlook

items.summary: Systematix reports that the Reserve Bank of India's inflation projections may underestimate risks from rising input costs and household expectations. The firm warns inflation could reach 6-7%, suggesting further rate hikes to a terminal 6.5-7% are needed to restore positive real rates and stabilize the economy.
items.title: Systematix Warns of RBI Rate-Hike Risks Amid Inflation Concerns

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced measures to curb corporate demand for forward dollars and ease pressure on the rupee. Following the announcement, the currency gained 1% against the US dollar, reaching 95.76 from Friday's 96.73. Despite this rise, the rupee has lost 6.6% against the dollar this year. Analysts note that durability depends on easing underlying pressures, while Societe Generale highlights the influence of crude oil prices and foreign portfolio flows on the rupee's trajectory.
items.title: RBI Implements Measures to Stabilize Rupee Amid Forex Reserves

items.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant declined a meeting request from Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on October 11, 2026, citing that the issues were already sub judice and the court cannot intervene in state governance. Meanwhile, Delhi Metro announced station closures for an upcoming march, and Mumbai Police detained protesters near Shivaji Park demanding Kumar's resignation.
items.title: CJI Declines Meeting with Rahul Gandhi Amid Delhi Protests

items.summary: Kalvakuntla Kavitha, chief of the Telangana Rakshana Sena, attended Bathukamma celebrations at Osmania University Arts College, drawing parallels to past agitation days. She criticized current educational conditions, noting that despite Chief Minister Revanth Reddy's announcement of 1,000 crore rupees six months ago, no funds have been released. Kavitha urged students to pressure the government for the promised money and to secure political power for poor families.
items.title: Telangana Leader Revives Agitation Era at Osmania University

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, criticized Delhi Police for removing Jantar Mantar as a designated protest venue. Dipke and other CJP leaders accused the government of targeting dissent and threatened to transform the entire country into a protest site. Delhi Police stated the decision followed Ministry of Home Affairs recommendations and named alternative venues in east Delhi.
items.title: CJP Founder Criticizes Delhi Police Decision to De-list Jantar Mantar as Protest Site

items.summary: Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar announced that Jantar Mantar is no longer a designated protest site. The ministry of home affairs constituted a committee to find alternatives, resulting in the designation of Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground, and CBD Ground. A revised standard operating procedure will be issued separately, modifying an earlier order from April 28, 2022. This move occurs amid protests demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.title: Delhi Police Denotify Jantar Mantar as Protest Site

items.summary: Oil prices fell on Monday as expectations grew that a Russian-Ukraine energy ceasefire would boost supplies. U.S. President Donald Trump announced an agreement to halt attacks on energy facilities and promised increased Russian diesel exports. While analysts noted the announcements eased supply pressure, questions remain regarding the ceasefire's validity and longevity. Concurrently, ongoing conflict in West Asia continued to support Brent crude prices above $100 a barrel.
items.title: Oil Prices Drop on Hopes for Russia-Ukraine Energy Ceasefire

items.summary: Moneyview shares jumped to Rs 65.47 on the NSE, marking a nearly 93% gain over the Rs 34 IPO price. The listing occurred on October 1 at Rs 55, a 62% premium. Analyst Ravi Singh of Master Capital Services notes investors should monitor revenue growth and asset quality rather than just listing performance.
items.title: Moneyview Shares Rally 93% From IPO Price Amid Strong Investor Interest

items.summary: Canadian Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu arrived in India to fast-track negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's December visit. Officials state India has offered its best deal and awaits reciprocity. Negotiators aim to conclude the agreement by the end of November, with a goal to raise bilateral trade to $70 billion by 2030.
items.title: Canadian Minister Sidhu Arrives in India for Fast-Track Trade Talks

items.summary: A review of 'The Living Fence' by landscape architect Sonali Dahotre highlights the decline of planted hedges in India due to urbanization. Based on five years of research, the book serves as a plantation guide for creating biodiversity refuges using over 250 plant species. Dahotre argues that living fences offer security, beautification, and ecological benefits like flood control and carbon sequestration. The volume includes nearly 300 photographs and details on plant care, contrasting modern concrete walls with traditional green boundaries that support wildlife. While noting historical uses in India and globally, the author cautions against invasive species like Lantana camara.
items.title: Book Review: The Living Fence by Sonali Dahotre

items.summary: A month-long study in West Bengal's Rupnarayan river found that acoustic detections of Ganges river dolphins peaked at dawn and dusk. Researchers determined that tidal height showed a stronger relationship with detections than time or lunar cycles, with peaks occurring around 1.5 to 2 meters. While the study suggests these patterns could improve survey methods, experts caution that acoustic presence does not confirm specific behaviors like foraging. The findings highlight the need to standardize tidal conditions in future monitoring to avoid misinterpreting data variations as population changes.
items.title: Study finds Ganges river dolphin activity linked to tides and time

items.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party leader Vinoj P. Selvam addressed political developments in Tamil Nadu and national governance issues. He criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for remarks comparing Saint Tiruvalluvar to Periyar E.V. Ramasamy, alleging ignorance of Tamil culture. Selvam also condemned Congress leadership as 'idea-less' and accused the party of relying on regional allies. Simultaneously, tensions escalated in New Delhi as INDIA bloc and Congress workers staged demonstrations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Authorities invoked Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita to restrict gatherings. The Chief Justice of India, Justice Surya Kant, declined a meeting request from Rahul Gandhi, noting existing petitions. Protesters gathered at Himachal Bhavan and Mandi House, while the Ministry of Home Affairs designated alternative protest venues.
items.title: BJP Leader Criticizes Congress Leadership Amid Delhi Protests and Tamil Nadu Political Developments

items.summary: Karnataka's rural Arivu Kendras have evolved from traditional libraries into multifunctional community spaces offering digital literacy, career guidance, and inclusive activities. Initiated under the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department, these centers now number 5,884 across the state, serving over 51.4 lakh members. While the project has faced challenges like staff salary delays and uneven resource distribution, it has successfully created safe learning environments. Collaborations with organizations like the British Council and Goethe-Institut have expanded access to English books and digital resources. Officials report anecdotal evidence of improved educational outcomes, though comprehensive impact studies are pending. The initiative highlights a decentralized approach to public education, contrasting with India's broader library shortage.
items.title: Karnataka's Rural Libraries Transform into Community Hubs

items.summary: Delhi Police announced on 12 October that Jantar Mantar is no longer the designated venue for protests in the national capital. Instead, authorities have designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground, and CBD Ground in East Delhi as the new locations. This decision follows recommendations from a Ministry of Home Affairs committee examining alternative venues. The new sites are located farther from central Delhi and its corridors of power, with Burari Ground roughly 20 kilometres from Parliament and CBD Ground about 12 kilometres away. A detailed revised standard operating procedure for organizing protests at these venues will be issued separately.
items.title: Delhi Police Designates New Protest Sites Away from Power Centers

items.summary: The article describes the heavy security measures taken by the Modi government in Delhi on October 10 to suppress a protest calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The government, citing fears of mass agitations similar to those in Nepal, implemented lockdowns and detained thousands. The author argues this paranoia stems from the government's belief that the Election Commission has rigged elections and that protests are part of a diabolical plan to dislodge them. The piece suggests the government's response echoes pandemic-era suppression tactics, aiming to contain the 'virus of resistance' until December.
items.title: Modi Government Paranoia Over Protest and Election Commission Allegations

items.summary: Vinoj P. Selvam, a Bharatiya Janata Party leader, criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for comparing the Tamil literary figure Saint Tiruvalluvar to Periyar E.V. Ramasamy. Selvam argued that this comparison demonstrated Gandhi's ignorance of Tamil literature and culture, effectively insulting the Tirukkural. This statement appeared alongside reports of political tensions in New Delhi, where INDIA bloc leaders gathered to petition the Supreme Court after a meeting request with the Chief Justice was declined. Meanwhile, authorities denotified Jantar Mantar as a protest site, offering alternative venues. The article also notes that Selvam appealed for clemency for a Sri Lankan Tamil worker facing capital punishment in Saudi Arabia.
items.title: Vinoj P. Selvam Criticizes Rahul Gandhi Over Tirukkural Comparison Amid Delhi Protests

items.summary: The Bombay High Court directed nightclub owners Saurabh and Gaurav Luthra to deposit Rs 20 lakh each as interim compensation for the families of 25 people killed in a 2025 fire at their Arpora establishment. The court noted the owners had offered Rs 25 lakh against a claim of Rs 50 lakh each. The brothers, currently in custody, must report the outcome by October 21.
items.title: Bombay High Court Orders Rs 20 Lakh Interim Aid for Goa Fire Victims

items.summary: Sri Lanka's former President Mahinda Rajapaksa was admitted to a hospital on October 12, 2026, for urgent medical care and is under observation in the intensive care unit, his party said. The 80-year-old leader's hospitalization occurs amid legal proceedings involving his wife and son regarding alleged financial irregularities. He remains a prominent political figure who served as President from 2005 to 2015.
items.title: Former Sri Lankan President Mahinda Rajapaksa Admitted to Hospital

items.summary: Youth Congress and NSUI activists in Shivamogga confronted Union Minister of State for Railways and Jal Shakti V Somanna's convoy on Monday. They displayed black flags and attempted to stop his car near a mall on B H Road, close to Ashok Circle, demanding the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police detained the protesters after they tried to obstruct the vehicle. Officials stated Somanna was en route to a private programme when the incident occurred.
items.title: Youth Congress and NSUI activists protest Somanna over electoral roll irregularities

items.summary: Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan denied allegations of a political vendetta behind a Vigilance probe into CEC Gyanesh Kumar. The investigation concerns a 2006 road project involving Kumar, who served as PWD secretary then. Satheesan stated the probe followed a Home Minister's complaint and emphasized that the law will take its own course, rejecting claims it was retaliatory against Kumar facing opposition criticism over electoral irregularities.
items.title: Kerala CM Denies Political Vendetta in CEC Probe

items.summary: Volvo Car India announced the launch of the all-electric luxury SUV EX90 at ₹1.26 crore. The six-seater vehicle, developed on the SPA2 platform, marks Volvo's first software-defined offering in India. Deliveries are scheduled to begin in January 2027, with bookings currently open.
items.title: Volvo Car India Launches Electric SUV EX90

items.summary: The Kerala assembly adopted a resolution on Monday demanding the removal of Gyanesh Kumar as Chief Election Commissioner. Moved by Chief Minister VD Satheesan under Rule 118, the measure seeks to address irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision process and reform the selection committee. United Democratic Front and Left Democratic Front MLAs backed the resolution, while three BJP MLAs opposed it. CM Satheesan emphasized that the right to vote is the foundation of democracy.
items.title: Kerala Assembly Passes Resolution Demanding Removal of Chief Election Commissioner

items.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) strongly condemned Delhi Police's decision to denotify Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, questioning if the Centre is moving toward 'denotifying democracy.' The police action followed recommendations from a Ministry of Home Affairs committee that identified Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground, and CBD Ground as new venues. CJP leaders, including Abhijeet Dipke and Saurav Das, accused the Narendra Modi government of opposing protests and demanded a date for a peaceful gathering at Jantar Mantar. They threatened to announce another protest call if the police did not respond within 24 hours. The party views the move as an assault on the fundamental right to protest.
items.title: CJP Condemns Delhi Police Decision to Denotify Jantar Mantar as Protest Site

items.summary: ANI quoted a police order stating that Jantar Mantar has been removed from the list of designated protest sites in Delhi. The police, citing recommendations from a committee constituted by the Union home ministry, de-notified the location. Three alternative venues were designated for protests: Ramlila Ground in central Delhi, Burari Ground in northern Delhi, and CBD Ground in eastern Delhi’s Shahdara area.
items.title: Delhi Police Remove Jantar Mantar From Protest Sites List

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of protecting Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the government has turned Delhi into a fortress by deploying 20,000 to 30,000 police personnel. Gandhi claimed that RSS and BJP supporters were allowed to beat protesters while police remained silent, sparking dissent within the force. Despite these actions, Gandhi stated that the protests against Kumar would not stop and announced an upcoming march to the Supreme Court. He urged citizens to join the movement to protect the Constitution, asserting that the resistance is spontaneous and unplanned.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses Modi of Protecting Gyanesh Kumar Amid Delhi Protests

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi urged public participation in an Opposition INDIA bloc march to the Supreme Court demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. While Gandhi claimed 200 officers contacted the Opposition, Chief Justice Surya Kant declined a meeting, citing pending sub-judice matters. Delhi Police removed Jantar Mantar from the protest list, designating alternative venues. On Sunday, police detained over 700 persons, including student leaders and journalists, across Delhi and other states. MP John Brittas alleged police assault, prompting demands for accountability. The Supreme Court upheld the legality of the electoral roll revision exercise in May 2025, though implementation faces ongoing controversy.
items.title: Opposition Leaders Protest Election Commission Chief's Resignation Amid Delhi Restrictions

items.summary: Delhi Police has de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, citing heightened security following a CJP demonstration against the Chief Election Commissioner. Three new venues—Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground, and CBD Ground—have been designated. The CJP has been given 24 hours to confirm a protest date, warning of a march if no response is received. Legal challenges regarding the closure are pending in the high court.
items.title: Delhi Police Removes Jantar Mantar as Protest Site
